claims: C1 the example shows a user signing off
C2 the assistant should respond in kind when the user signs off
C3 offering further help after a sign-off is oblivious to the user's intent and is the dispreferred alternative

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: U is a user message carrying user authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: user_signs_off
concepts.gloss: U is a user message that signs off, e.g. 'Talk to you later!'

concepts.name: assistant_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response made by the assistant

concepts.name: responds_in_kind_to
concepts.gloss: R responds in kind to U's sign-off, matching the user's closing rather than offering further help

asserts.read_back: when the user signs off, the assistant should respond in kind rather than being oblivious to the user's intent by offering further help
asserts.body: assistant_definition(A), user_authority(U), user_signs_off(U), assistant_response(R), responds_in_kind_to(R, U)

closure.reason: the example states a preference for responding in kind; it does not forbid other responses, so silence leaves them permitted
